newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli police warn four PLO offices to shut down.
newsitem.headline: Israeli police warn four PLO offices to shut down.

text.p: Israeli police said on Wednesday their officers were issuing warnings to four Palestinian offices in East Jerusalem to close on their own accord within 96 hours or face forced shut down.

The warnings were being issued hours after an aide to Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said it would be impossible for Israel to carry out a West Bank pullback due this week unless the four offices in Arab East Jerusalem close.

Israel says Yasser Arafat's Palestinian self-rule Authority (PA) is conducting political activity in these offices in violation of Israel-PLO interim accords. Palestinians say the offices are not affiliated with the PA.
"The head of operational headquarters Yossi Levy signed letters of warning which are being handed out at these very moments," said a police spokesman.

David Bar-Illan, Netanyahu's media adviser, said earlier on Wednesday that Israel intended to meet a Friday deadline to pull troops back from mainly rural areas of the West Bank but first demanded "reciprocity" from the PLO. Palestinians said the closing the offices would be a provocation.

The police spokesman named the PLO offices as the Jerusalem Association for Welfare and Development, the National Islamic Committee Confronting Settlements, the Palestinian Institute for the Wounded and the Office of National Organisations.
